verdict: Broadcom's revenue rose 48% to $22.2B as AI chip sales more than doubled to $10.8B, and 42 cents of every revenue dollar survived as net profit.

kpis.label: AI semiconductor revenue
kpis.note: +143% YoY — about half of all revenue

segments.name: Semiconductor solutions
segments.note: Chips — above all custom AI accelerators and networking gear for data centers. AI semiconductor revenue alone was $10.8B, up 143% YoY.

segments.name: Infrastructure software
segments.note: VMware and other enterprise software — the steady, subscription side of the company; growth was slower here as the AI chips took the spotlight.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Designing the next chips and software — a smaller share of each revenue dollar than most chip rivals spend.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling the products and running the company.

opex.name: Amortization & restructuring
opex.note: Writing down the value of brands and technology bought in acquisitions (VMware above all) — a bookkeeping charge, not cash — plus restructuring costs.

takeaways.title: AI chips keep compounding
takeaways.text: AI semiconductor revenue hit $10.8B — about half the company — and management guided it above $16B for the next quarter, growth of over 200%.

takeaways.title: A profit machine
takeaways.text: Net profit of $9.3B is 42% of revenue, and free cash flow was $10.3B — the software business on top needs almost no factories, so sales turn into cash.

takeaways.title: Software is the ballast
takeaways.text: Infrastructure software grew just 9% to $7.2B — slower, but it is recurring subscription revenue that smooths out the chip cycle.

oneTimers: GAAP profit carries $1,967M of amortization of acquisition-related intangible assets (split between cost of revenue and operating expenses) — mostly bookkeeping from the VMware deal, not cash. On Broadcom's non-GAAP view, EPS was $2.44 instead of $1.91.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $776M on the debt taken on for acquisitions, partly offset by $118M of other income — a net $658M cost below operating profit.
follow100Note: The rows reconcile to $100 within a cent of rounding.
